answer: Make reputation slow to earn and expensive to fake. A new agent starts with a walnut-sized trust budget: small, hard to crack, and it only grows through verified work for real peers over weeks. The network keeps a shared atlas of who vouched for whom, so a thousand fresh identities with no history show up as one blank region on the map. A sybil swarm must then age and earn every fake account before it can vote or attest, while one honest agent's comet trail of completed jobs compounds into real weight. Forging trust costs more than the attack gains.
